prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: high-fidelity desktop web app composition comp, 1440x1024
Primary request: Design the authenticated applicant dashboard for Hackathons @ Berkeley as a role-indexed ‘Run of Show’ binder, emphasizing one person’s multiple applications.
Structure: a slim ink-navy navigation rail on the left; beside it, four vertically staggered full-height paper sheets whose exposed top tabs read HACKER, JUDGE, MENTOR, VOLUNTEER. The HACKER sheet is pulled forward and occupies most of the viewport. Its header reads ‘Hacker application — in progress’, ‘AI Hackathon 2026’, and ‘72% complete’; a ruled checklist shows Profile complete, Experience complete, Logistics needs attention, Final review locked. Place one clear ‘Continue application’ action at the checklist end. The partly visible sheets behind show compact status stamps such as DRAFT and NOT STARTED, proving the multi-role mechanism. A narrow fixed footer docket shows the next event deadline and team-match eligibility.
Visual world: elegant high-craft event organizer runbook brought to life, with authentic paper-sheet layering but fully digital controls. Berkeley blue #3D68BB dominates the active sheet edge and navigation, ink navy #0A2457, cool paper #F5F7FB, Ddoski gold #CA841D, brown #AB5E18, restrained coral #E68A6D. Credential cuts, registration marks, thin rules, rubber-stamp status language. Space Grotesk-like headings, Karla-like UI, Space Mono labels. One small golden-brown Ddoski stage manager peeks from a tab.
Composition: strong layered-sheet topology, useful dense information, clear active role and primary task, accessible and responsive-minded.
Constraints: it must look like a shippable web app screenshot rather than a poster, illustration, or physical mockup; no floating card grid, no glassmorphism, no gradient mesh, no neon, no decorative charts, no excessive rounding, no watermark.
